title: Only 7% Pass This University Entrance Exam
summary: Reasoning challenges and disguised study-style decisions build your worldwide university match across 10 admissions rounds.

landing.intro: Put your skills to the test, earn your entrance score and discover which world-leading university would accept you.

about.body:
This 60-question university entrance challenge moves from accessible warm-ups into verbal, quantitative and scientific reasoning, evidence analysis, worldwide knowledge and practical problem-solving. Every interaction is scored, so the final percentage reflects your answers across all ten stages.

Your university match is calculated from the shape of your academic strengths. Different top-tier institutions emphasise different combinations of language, numbers, science, critical analysis, global awareness and applied problem-solving, so two people with the same total score can receive different matches.

The questions use worldwide English and do not depend on any country’s school curriculum or admissions system. Real admission decisions use qualifications, applications, references, interviews and institution-specific requirements that this entertainment quiz cannot assess.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Answer all six scored questions in each entrance-exam stage.
Use only the information shown; speed never affects your score.
Complete all ten stages to reveal your percentage, strongest subject area and top-tier university match.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment only. This quiz is not affiliated with any university, does not assess eligibility and cannot predict an admissions decision.

profiles.title: OXFORD
profiles.copy: You thrive when a difficult idea is challenged from every angle. Your mix of verbal reasoning, critical thought and self-directed curiosity suits an intense tutorial-style environment.

profiles.title: CAMBRIDGE
profiles.copy: You bring patience and structure to complex scientific and numerical problems. You appear happiest when a rigorous method leads toward a deeper independent discovery.

profiles.title: HARVARD
profiles.copy: You connect knowledge with people, context and practical influence. Your broad perspective and appetite for discussion point toward a highly collaborative, outward-looking environment.

profiles.title: MIT
profiles.copy: You turn rules, numbers and constraints into things that work. Your profile combines technical discipline with the urge to test, build and improve.

profiles.title: STANFORD
profiles.copy: You are drawn to useful ideas with room to grow. Your strongest match rewards experimentation, initiative and connecting technical thinking with real-world impact.

profiles.title: YALE
profiles.copy: You notice the meaning behind arguments and communicate ideas with clarity. Discussion, breadth and a strong sense of wider context shape your result.

profiles.title: PRINCETON
profiles.copy: You prefer depth over noise and are willing to stay with a hard problem. Precision, independent thought and carefully constructed arguments drive this match.

profiles.title: IMPERIAL COLLEGE LONDON
profiles.copy: You combine scientific reasoning with a practical urge to solve consequential problems. Technical focus and an international outlook make this a natural match.

profiles.title: ETH ZURICH
profiles.copy: You value exact methods, strong quantitative reasoning and solutions that survive close inspection. Your profile is systematic, independent and technically ambitious.

profiles.title: NATIONAL UNIVERSITY OF SINGAPORE
profiles.copy: You connect knowledge to practical challenges across cultures and systems. Adaptability, global perspective and collaborative leadership define this match.

match.disclaimer: For entertainment only. This quiz is not affiliated with any university, does not assess eligibility and cannot predict an admissions decision. Your match is based only on your pattern across these general reasoning questions.

questions.question: BOOK is to READING as FORK is to…
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Eating.

questions.question: What comes next: 4, 7, 10, 13, ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 16.

questions.question: Which change would make ice melt fastest?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Break it into smaller pieces.

questions.question: All lorens are silver. This object is a loren. What follows?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is It is silver.

questions.question: Which continent contains the most countries?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Africa.

questions.question: Four interviews take 25 minutes each with 5-minute gaps. How long from the first start to the last finish?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 115 minutes.

questions.question: Which word best completes: evidence, analysis, ___, conclusion?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Interpretation.

questions.question: Which pair has the same relationship as QUESTION : ANSWER?
questions.explanation: A solution resolves a problem in the same way that an answer resolves a question.

questions.question: COMPASS is to DIRECTION as THERMOMETER is to…
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Temperature.

questions.question: Which word can follow both TERM and RESEARCH?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Paper.

questions.question: The committee called the proposal coherent. What does coherent most nearly mean?
questions.explanation: Coherent means that the ideas form a clear, logically connected whole.

questions.question: Which conclusion is best supported?
answers: Longer opening hours did not increase attendance
questions.context: The museum extended its opening hours, but visitor numbers stayed unchanged.
questions.explanation: The passage supports only the limited conclusion that the longer hours did not increase visitor numbers.

questions.question: A fee rises from 80 to 100. What is the percentage increase?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 25%.

questions.question: A class of 40 has 24 students studying science. What fraction is that?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 3/5.

questions.question: A value doubles, then 6 is subtracted, giving 18. What was the value?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 12.

questions.question: Three numbers average 18. Two are 14 and 20. What is the third?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 20.

questions.question: A course has 18 places. Two-thirds are filled. How many places remain?
questions.explanation: Two-thirds of 18 is 12, leaving 6 places.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?
answers: Group A had the higher pass rate
Both groups had a 75% pass rate
Group B had the higher pass rate
questions.context: Group A: 24 applicants, 18 passed. Group B: 16 applicants, 12 passed.
questions.explanation: 18 out of 24 and 12 out of 16 both equal 75%.

questions.question: A plant bends toward a window. What best explains this?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Light affects growth.

questions.question: Which observation best supports that air has mass?
answers: An inflated ball weighs more than an empty one
questions.explanation: The correct answer is An inflated ball weighs more than an empty one.

questions.question: Why does a metal spoon feel colder than a wooden spoon in the same room?
answers: Metal is at a lower temperature
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Metal conducts heat away faster.

questions.question: Which design best tests whether light affects plant growth?
answers: Identical plants with different light levels
Two plant types in different soil
Different plants in the same light
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Identical plants with different light levels.

questions.question: Which design best isolates whether fertiliser affects seedling growth?
answers: Use different plants in different rooms
Give every plant a different amount of water
Keep light and water equal; vary only fertiliser
Compare one young plant with one mature plant
questions.explanation: A fair test changes only the factor being investigated while keeping other conditions equal.

questions.question: Which observation best supports the conclusion that heating expanded the ball?
answers: The ball looked brighter when hot
The hot ball no longer passed, but passed again after cooling
The ball and ring had the same colour
questions.context: A metal ball passes through a ring when cool. After heating, it does not pass.
questions.explanation: The reversible change—failing when hot and passing after cooling—supports thermal expansion.

questions.question: A study finds two things rise together. What can you safely conclude?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is They are associated.

questions.question: A speaker gives one vivid example and claims it proves a universal rule. What is the weakness?
answers: One case may not represent all cases
questions.explanation: The correct answer is One case may not represent all cases.

questions.question: A survey asks only satisfied customers. What is the clearest problem?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is The sample is biased.

questions.question: If a rule has one confirmed exception, which claim must be false?
answers: The rule applies in many cases
questions.explanation: The correct answer is The rule applies without exception.

questions.question: A headline says a treatment 'may help' but the article says it was tested on 12 people. What is the most careful response?
answers: The finding is promising but limited
questions.explanation: The correct answer is The finding is promising but limited.

questions.question: What most weakens the claim that the practice test caused the improvement?
answers: There was no comparison group, and other preparation may explain it
questions.context: Everyone who completed a practice test improved. The committee says the practice test caused the improvement.
questions.explanation: Without a comparison group, other preparation could account for the improvement.

questions.question: Which language has the most native speakers worldwide?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Mandarin Chinese.

questions.question: The Andes mountain range is primarily in which continent?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is South America.

questions.question: Which ocean is the largest?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Pacific.

questions.question: Which organisation has member countries from every inhabited continent?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is United Nations.

questions.question: Which country lies in both Europe and Asia?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Türkiye.

questions.question: Which continent is crossed by both the Equator and the Prime Meridian?
questions.explanation: Both zero degrees latitude and zero degrees longitude cross Africa.

questions.question: A project requires 12 person-hours. Two people divide the work evenly and work at the same speed. What is the minimum completion time?
questions.explanation: Twelve person-hours divided equally between two people requires 6 hours.

questions.question: A device fails only when it gets hot. What is the best first test?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Compare it at controlled temperatures.

questions.question: A queue grows by 8 people every 10 minutes. Two extra desks together serve 12 people every 10 minutes. What happens?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is It shrinks by 4.

questions.question: A hall seats 120. Groups of 18 arrive. What is the largest number of complete groups that fit?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 6.

questions.question: What is the shortest time in which all four checks can finish?
questions.context: Checks A and B take 10 minutes each; C and D take 20. Two people can work at the same time.
questions.explanation: Each person can take one 10-minute and one 20-minute check, so both finish after 30 minutes.

questions.question: Which schedule obeys every dependency?
questions.context: Research must happen before Draft. Draft must happen before Review. Design can happen at any time.
questions.explanation: Research must precede Draft, and Draft must precede Review; Design may occur between them.

questions.question: Opposite of SCARCE?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Abundant.

questions.question: Which number breaks the rule?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 48.

questions.question: What carries genetic instructions?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is DNA.

questions.question: Can one example prove a universal rule?
questions.explanation: A single example can support a possibility, but it cannot establish a universal rule.

questions.question: Which line marks 0° latitude?
questions.explanation: The Equator is the line of zero degrees latitude.

questions.question: Best first fix for a slipping deadline?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Identify the bottleneck.

questions.question: Which sentence is the strongest claim?
questions.context: Four conclusions are proposed from the same limited evidence.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is This always improves results.

questions.question: How does the final price compare with the original?
questions.context: A price falls by 20%, then rises by 20%.
questions.explanation: Starting from 100 gives 80 after the reduction, then 96 after a 20% increase: 4% below the original.

questions.question: What happens to the air pressure?
questions.context: A sealed syringe of air is compressed while temperature stays constant.
questions.explanation: Compressing the same amount of gas into less space at constant temperature increases its pressure.

questions.question: Which fact most weakens the headline’s claim?
answers: Traffic was measured for six months
Remote work increased and fuel prices rose during the same period
questions.context: Six months after cycle lanes were added, traffic was lower. A headline says the lanes caused all of the reduction.
questions.explanation: Two major changes occurred at the same time, so the cycle lanes cannot be credited with the entire drop.

questions.question: What is true about the two points?
answers: They are equally far from the Equator
Point A is farther from the Equator
Point B is farther from the Equator
They are on the same latitude
questions.context: MAP COORDINATES: Point A is 20°N. Point B is 20°S.
questions.explanation: Twenty degrees north and twenty degrees south are equal angular distances from the Equator.

questions.question: How many booklets are produced in total?
questions.context: A printer makes 30 booklets in 6 minutes. Two identical printers start together, but one stops after 3 minutes.
questions.explanation: Each printer makes 5 booklets per minute. One makes 30 in six minutes and the other makes 15 in three: 45 total.

questions.question: Which revision accurately reflects both facts?
answers: The plan is cheap in every respect
The plan costs little initially but may be expensive over time
The plan should be rejected immediately
questions.context: The report calls the plan affordable because its initial cost is low. It later notes that annual maintenance is expensive.
questions.explanation: The best revision preserves both the low initial cost and the high continuing cost.

questions.question: A scholarship fund is split 2:3 between two projects. The larger project receives 36,000. What is the total fund?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 60,000.

questions.question: A sealed-jar plant remains healthy in light but declines in darkness. Which explanation uses both observations?
answers: Light enables photosynthesis, while respiration continues in both
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Light enables photosynthesis, while respiration continues in both.

questions.question: Every shortlisted proposal has evidence. Some proposals with evidence are rejected. What must be true?
answers: Evidence alone does not guarantee acceptance
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Evidence alone does not guarantee acceptance.

questions.question: An interview begins at 09:00 UTC and lasts 90 minutes. What local time does it finish at UTC+5:30?
questions.explanation: The interview ends at 10:30 UTC. Adding 5 hours 30 minutes gives 16:00 local time.

questions.question: A team processes 100 files. Better accuracy prevents 15 errors, each costing 5 work-hours; a speed upgrade saves 20 work-hours. Which saves more work?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Accuracy, saving 75 hours.
